task.description: REWORK ITERATION 1: your prior attempt (step-03-elixir-dev.json) correctly stopped and reported that the original design's mechanism was mechanically infeasible rather than implementing something broken -- that was the right call, not a mistake, and this is not a rework of anything you did wrong. CODE-DESIGNER has since revised the design to Revision 2, a build-time skip/defer mechanism, and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently re-verified it against real Ecto.Multi semantics and PASSED it (see step-02b-regate-code-design-validator.json). Read the CURRENT lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md directly in full -- it is substantially different from what you read before (only build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3 changes to /4, adding a skip_task_activation?: boolean() parameter/predicate computed from prepared_children's already-known child_initial_state.status, decided before either Multi step is built). Implement this revised design exactly. If you find this revision is ALSO not mechanically sound once you're implementing it, stop and report that again rather than diverging -- but the design gate this time included an independent verification of the exact class of problem that broke the first attempt, so this should be implementable as specified.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation matches the REVISED design's signature change exactly (build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3 -> /4 with the skip predicate, as specified in the current design doc)
A synchronously-completing SUB_PROCESS child no longer raises Ecto.Multi.merge_results/3's key-collision RuntimeError (verify with an ad-hoc/throwaway check before finishing, not just by inspection)
The async/queued SUB_PROCESS completion path's existing behavior is unchanged (no existing test in test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs or test/letflow/engine_test.exs regresses)
No implementation deviates from the approved design without being flagged explicitly as an issue in result.issues

result.summary:
Implemented Revision 2 of lib/letflow/design/iss0392-multi-task-records-collision-fix.md exactly as specified -- the build-time skip/defer mechanism, not the mechanically-infeasible Revision 1 replace mechanism the prior attempt correctly stopped on. Confirmed current source matched the design's own line citations before editing (engine.ex:2412/2415 parent_instance_id binding and call site, engine.ex:2572-2592 build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3's body, sub_process.ex prepare_child_activation/4's child_initial_state.status shape) -- all matched, no drift from what CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR verified.

Changes, both in lib/letflow/engine.ex only (no other file needed changes -- confirmed via git status --short after implementation, matching the design's own narrow scope claim in §2.5):

1. build_complete_task_tail_multi/6's second clause (engine.ex, the {:advanced, ...} branch): immediately after parent_instance_id is bound, computes skip_task_activation? = Enum.any?(prepared_children, fn {_id, prepared} -> prepared.child_initial_state.status == :completed end), per design §2.2's predicate stated in prose. Threads it into build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3 -> /4 as the new 4th argument. No other part of the pipe changed.

2. build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi/3 -> /4: gained skip_task_activation? :: boolean() as specified in design §2.5. Delegates the conditional to a new private helper, maybe_append_task_activation_multi/7 (two clauses, pattern-matched on the boolean), which either omits TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6 entirely (skip_task_activation? true) or calls it exactly as before (false). Return type unchanged (bare Multi.t()). reconcile_token_records/5's own :token_reconciliation step is untouched, called unconditionally in both cases, matching design §2.4's 'only the task-activation sub-step is conditionally omitted' instruction.

No signature changed for append_sub_process_children_creation_multi/6, SubProcess.append_start_multi/7, maybe_chain_synchronous_completion/6, append_completion_multi/5, build_completion_write_steps/12, maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6, or TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6 -- all confirmed unchanged in the diff, matching design §2.5/§3.2's explicit withdrawal of Revision 1's five-function signature chain. This mechanism IS mechanically sound as implemented: the predicate is evaluated once, in plain Elixir, before either Multi step exists, so no Ecto.Multi step is ever built-then-replaced.

Verification performed (not just inspection): wrote an ad-hoc throwaway test, scratch/iss0392_verify_fix_test.exs (deleted after running, NOT committed -- adapted directly from ISSUE-FIXER's own scratch/iss0392_repro_test.exs fixture, matching design §5's exact scenario: parent START->HUMAN_TASK('gate')->SUB_PROCESS('sp')->END, child START->END with no intervening task so it completes synchronously). Ran `mix test scratch/iss0392_verify_fix_test.exs`: 1 passed, 0 failures. Asserted and confirmed: Engine.complete_task/3 no longer raises (previously raised RuntimeError 'cannot merge Multi ... task_records'), returns {:ok, _}, the parent instance_projections row reaches status: :completed, and zero orphan :pending tasks rows remain for that instance -- i.e. call (1)'s step was never built, so there was no earlier-snapshot row to have inserted, exactly as design §5 point 6 predicts structurally (not merely arranged by timing).

Regression check: `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/engine_test.exs` -- 55 passed, 0 failures (72.6s). Full suite: `mix test` -- 3000 passed (6 properties, 2994 tests), 10 excluded, 0 failures (1503.6s), exit code 0. Async/queued SUB_PROCESS completion path (AC3) is unaffected by construction -- confirmed by design §4's own argument (a hop chain with only :active children never sets skip_task_activation? true) and empirically by the full suite passing with zero regressions across engine_sub_process_test.exs's existing async/queued-path test cases.

`mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, zero warnings. `mix format --check-formatted`: clean, no diff.

Cascade case (maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/6, design §3): correctly left untouched per the design -- its own build-time predicate cannot extend there (the ancestor lookup is execution-time-only via a locking DB read inside Multi.run/3), and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already independently verified this is a real mechanical limit, not a convenience deferral, and non-load-bearing for ISS-0392's own filed repro (single-level only). No implementation deviates from the approved design; nothing to flag in issues.
